video_title: La DURA HISTORIA de CARL HERRERA

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his pride in being a Venezuelan basketball pioneer
quotes.excerpt: My name is Carl Herrera, ex-basketball player, Venezuelan, very proud to be so.
quotes.quote: My name is Carl Herrera, ex-basketball player, Venezuelan, very proud to be so, and now venturing into NBA broadcasting.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Hola, mi nombre es Carl Herrera, ex-deportista de baloncesto venezolano, muy orgulloso de serlo, y ahora incursionando en el broadcasting de la NBA.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his deep connection to his Venezuelan roots
quotes.excerpt: My thoughts have always been of Venezuela. Since I started having a notion of life, my place was Venezuela.
quotes.quote: My thoughts have always been of Venezuela. Since I started having a notion of life, with my parents, when I could open my eyes and understand where I was, the place where I found myself was Venezuela.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Mis pensamientos, todos, han sido de Venezuela. Yo creo que desde que comencé a tener noción de la vida, con mis padres, cuando podía abrir los ojos y entender dónde estaba, el sitio donde me encontraba era Venezuela.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his early athletic development in Venezuela
quotes.excerpt: Everything started to change when I started to get involved in sports, in school.
quotes.quote: Everything started to change when I started to get involved in sports, in school. I started playing volleyball, well, first I started playing baseball, but not in an organized way, just as a hobby. Then I started practicing volleyball in school, there were inter-school tournaments, that was in La Pastora, Republic of Bolivia. There I did all my primary school, but that's where I started to get involved in sports.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Todo empezó a cambiar cuando sí empecé a incursionar en el deporte, en el colegio, empecé a jugar voleibol, bueno, primero comencé a jugar béisbol, pero no de manera organizada, sino por hobby. Luego empecé a practicar el voleibol en el colegio, se hacían intercursos, eso fue en La Pastora, República de Bolivia. Ahí hice toda la primaria, la hice allí, pero ahí fue donde empecé a hacer la parte deportiva.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his early basketball training in Venezuela
quotes.excerpt: I talked to some friends of mine to start teaching me to play basketball.
quotes.quote: I talked to some friends of mine to start teaching me to play basketball. They took me to the Subillaga Park, that's in Cotiza, and there they started to teach me how to run, where to take shots, from which side to defend.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Hablé con unos amigos míos para que me empezaran a enseñar a jugar baloncesto. Me llevaron al parque Subillaga, eso es en Cotiza, y ahí me empezaron a enseñar cómo se corría, dónde metía los tiros, de qué lado se defendía.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his rapid development as a young basketball player
quotes.excerpt: As I improved, I was invited to different selections, youth selections.
quotes.quote: As I improved, I was invited to different selections, youth selections. I also went to a selection of the Federal District when it was the Federal District with Néstor Salazar, Néstor Salazar, and things started to change.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: A medida que fui mejorando, me fueron invitando para diferentes selecciones, selecciones juvenil. Fui también a una selección de Distrito Federal cuando se llamaba Distrito Federal con Néstor Salazar, Néstor Salazar, y las cosas empezaron a cambiar.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on receiving a scholarship to play in the US
quotes.excerpt: Gabriel calls me after the game, we lost, he was playing with Pantera, I was playing with the Portuguese team.
quotes.quote: Gabriel calls me after the game, we lost, he was playing with Pantera, I was playing with the Portuguese team, and he tells me, 'Negrito, I have a surprise for you.' And I say, 'What happened?' He says, 'I have a scholarship, I have an I-20.' And I tell him, 'Gabriel, don't play with that, because you know that for a long time I've wanted to go to the United States.'
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Gabriel me llama después del partido, nos ganaron, él jugaba con Pantera, yo jugaba con el equipo Portuguesa, y me dice, 'Negrito, te tengo una sorpresa'. Y yo digo, '¿Qué pasó?'. Me dice, 'Te tengo una beca, te tengo una I-20'. Y yo le digo, 'Gabriel, no juegues con eso, porque tú sabes que yo desde hace tiempo me quiero ir a Estados Unidos'.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his difficult decision to leave Venezuela for the US
quotes.excerpt: On December 24, sitting in an airport and with the fear of leaving behind my own, Carl Herrera made the decision.
quotes.quote: On December 24, sitting in an airport and with the fear of leaving behind my own, Carl Herrera made the decision that changed his life. Without speaking English, without knowing exactly what awaited him, he got on a plane pushed by a scholarship and by the need to open a path. That trip, accompanied by strangers who appeared as angels, was the beginning of a career that carried the name of Venezuela to the world of basketball.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Un 24 de diciembre, sentado en un aeropuerto y con el miedo de dejar atrás a los suyos, Carl Herrera tomó la decisión que le cambió su vida. Sin hablar inglés, sin saber exactamente qué le esperaba, se montó en un avión empujado por una beca y por la necesidad de abrirse camino. Aquel viaje, acompañado por desconocidos que aparecieron como ángeles, fue el inicio de una carrera que llevó el nombre de Venezuela al baloncesto mundial.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on choosing to play for the Houston Cougars
quotes.excerpt: Larry at the end decides to go to UNLV with coach Jerry Tarkanian. I still hadn't signed.
quotes.quote: Larry at the end decides to go to UNLV with coach Jerry Tarkanian. I still hadn't signed, and I take three invitations from three universities: Oklahoma, UNLV for Larry Johnson, and Houston, the University of Houston Cougars.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Larry al final decide irse a UNLV con el entrenador Jerry Tarkanian. Yo todavía no había firmado, y tomo tres invitaciones de tres universidades: Oklahoma, UNLV por Larry Johnson, y Houston, la Universidad de Houston Cougars.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his role and team dynamics with the Houston Rockets
quotes.excerpt: Kenny Smith is the base of the team, the pilot, the one who handles the plane, the brain of the body.
quotes.quote: Kenny Smith is the base of the team, the pilot, the one who handles the plane, the brain of the body. He is there and will play these minutes. Maxwell plays this way, a bit crazy and all that, but he is the one who has the courage to be able to mark Jordan, to be able to mark those players who score a lot of points and we need them. Then we have Robert Horry, young, he is a good outside shooter, he has a high jumping potential. Then we have Otis Thorpe, who is the fourth strong player, puts a lot of screens, but marking players outside is a bit difficult for him. And then comes Hakeem Olajuwon, the star, everyone comes to see him play, he is the reference of the team. And then comes you, sixth man, I guarantee you 24 minutes of play, but I need you to mark whoever you have to mark, Karl Malone, Barkley, all those fourth players that you have to mark. Change the rhythm of the game. I don't need you to score 20 points, although I know you have the capacity to do it. Take rebounds, give screens, run the court and give yourself completely to the game.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Kenny Smith es el base del equipo, el piloto, el que maneja el avión, el cerebro del cuerpo. Él está y va a jugar estos minutos. Maxwell juega de esta forma, un poco alocado y todo eso, pero es el que tiene el coraje de poder marcar a Jordan, de poder marcar a esos jugadores que meten muchos puntos y los necesitamos. Luego tenemos a Robert Horry, joven, es un buen lanzador de afuera, tiene un potencial de salto muy alto. Luego tenemos a Otis Thorpe, que es el puesto cuatro fuerte, pone muchas cortinas, pero marcar jugadores de afuera se le hace un poco difícil. Y luego vienes tú, sexto hombre, yo te garantizo 24 minutos de juego, pero necesito que tú marques a quien tengas que marcar, Karl Malone, Barkley, todos esos puestos cuatro que tienes que marcar. Cambia el ritmo del juego. Yo no necesito que metas 20 puntos, aunque sé que tienes la capacidad de hacerlo. Toma rebotes, da cortinas, corre la cancha y entrégate completamente al juego.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on the significance of playing in the Olympics
quotes.excerpt: The biggest achievement was reaching the Olympics and representing my country.
quotes.quote: The biggest achievement was reaching the Olympics and representing my country. That was the biggest achievement.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: El logro más grande fue llegar a las Olimpiadas y representar a mi país. Ese fue el logro más grande.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on the difficulty of dealing with a traumatic injury
quotes.excerpt: no me la pudieron sacar, porque es más traumante tratarla de sacar que dejarla allí
quotes.quote: I think there are things that are written, and sometimes it is difficult to determine life in that way, and to say that there are things that are going to happen. But one never expects that kind of thing to happen. I think that not only being a reference for the country, in sports, but I think that no person should have something like that happen to them. And yes, it has been difficult for me, although I have forgotten, it has been forgotten, but when there are moments that I remember and I still have the bullet there, they couldn't take it out, because it is more traumatic to try to take it out than to leave it there.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Yo creo que hay cosas que están escritas, ¿no? Y y y y algunas veces es difícil determinar la vida de esa forma, ¿no? Y decir que que que hay cosas que que que van a pasar. Pero uno nunca se espera que que ese tipo de cosas pasen. Este, yo creo que no solamente siendo un referente del país, deportivo, pero es que yo creo que ninguna persona debería pasarle algo como eso. Este, y sí se me ha hecho difícil, aunque sí se me olvida, se me ha olvidado, pero cuando hay momentos que me acuerdo y yo tengo la bala ahí todavía. O sea, no me la pudieron sacar, porque es más traumante tratarla de sacar que dejarla allí.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his recovery and fear after being shot
quotes.excerpt: con miedo de salir, con miedo de hablarle a la gente, con miedo de que la gente se me acercara
quotes.quote: I did not know if I was going to live, with fear of going out, with fear of talking to people, with fear that people would approach me. The first thing I did was go to church when I left there, to thank God and the Virgin, because that happened in Margarita.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: No sabía si iba a vivir, este, con miedo de salir, con miedo de hablarle a la gente, con miedo de que la gente se me acercara. Lo primero que hice fue ir a la iglesia cuando salí de ahí, darle gracias a Dios y a la Virgen, porque eso pasó en Margarita.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on setting boundaries with fans after his injury
quotes.excerpt: hubo mucha gente que se molestó conmigo, pues yo en un momento que yo les decía que no daba autógrafos
quotes.quote: There were many people who were upset with me, because at one point I told them that I did not give autographs, that I did not give them, but as time went by, I went as if not overcoming, but managing.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Hubo mucha gente que se molestó conmigo, pues yo en un momento que yo les decía que no daba autógrafos, que no lo daba, pero al ir pasando el tiempo lo fui como que no superando, pero sí manejando.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on changing the work mentality in Venezuelan basketball
quotes.excerpt: cambiar la mentalidad de trabajo, entendiendo en un equipo se hacen las cosas
quotes.quote: First, change the work mentality, understanding that in a team things are done. Those opportunities that internationally, because of my image, because of knowledge, because of achievements, can also be done. And when I say that, the opportunities are not only for the athletes, opportunities for all the coaches, opportunities for exchanges at an international level.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Primero, cambiar la mentalidad de trabajo, entendiendo en un equipo se hacen las cosas. Esas oportunidades que a nivel internacional, por mi imagen, por conocimientos, por logros, también se pueden hacer. Y cuando digo eso, las oportunidades no solamente para los atletas, oportunidad para todos los entrenadores, este, las oportunidades de de de de intercambios a nivel internacional.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on the importance of hope and humility
quotes.excerpt: los sueños se cumplen siempre y cuando con humildad uno acepte las cosas
quotes.quote: I think that hopes are always going to be there. One can never stop having hope, of wanting to do things. Dreams are fulfilled as long as with humility one accepts the things, the environment in which you are, your parents, if you have your two parents with you or one or so, they are your references, they are what will not want bad for you, they are what will always fight for you to be well.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Yo creo que las esperanzas siempre van a estar ahí, ¿no? Uno nunca puede dejar de de de de de de tener esperanzas, de de querer hacer cosas, este, los sueños se cumplen siempre y cuando con humildad uno acepte las cosas, este, el el entorno en el cual estás, tus padres que si si tienes tus dos padres contigo o uno o así, son tus referentes, son lo que no van a querer mal para ti, son lo que siempre van a luchar para que tú estés bien.
